name: row-list
description:
A list of rows that share a shape: a fixed leading column, a name that shrinks, and something on the trailing edge. Two units were this — a ranked board and a credential list — and they shared their grid, their overflow rule and their reason for existing. What differed was the tag and what sits at each end, which is a variant.

The leading column is the whole reason the rows are a grid and not flex: a rank of 9 and 10 must stack without shifting the name beside them, and a `::marker` cannot be given a width.

base.$description:
CONTAINER. This unit establishes an inline-size container named after itself, so anything inside it can respond to the width of THIS BOX rather than to the width of the window. That is the difference that matters for a design system: a composite dropped into a 320px sidebar and the same composite on a 320px phone are the same situation, and a viewport query calls them different ones. The library carries no viewport media query anywhere for exactly this reason — the only `@media` in it is `prefers-reduced-motion`, which is a person's setting and not a size.

`inline-size: 100%` is the container's REQUIRED companion, not a preference. `container-type: inline-size` makes the box's width independent of its contents — that is the containment being asked for — so a container with no width of its own has nothing left to size from and collapses to zero. This unit did: centred in a grid it became a column of single words. A container fills what it is given and bounds itself with `max-inline-size`; it never sizes to its text.

TEXT-ALIGN: START, declared rather than inherited. A list dropped into a centred container centres, and a centred list of rows has as many left edges as it has rows — the same argument claim-card's benefit list makes. This surfaced the moment row-list was used inside flow-card, which centres its body.

lead.$description: The fixed column — a rank, an icon, a checkbox. Right-aligned and tabular so 9 and 10 stack rather than shifting the name.

name.$description: Arbitrary user text — a device name, a claimed name. `overflow-wrap:anywhere` because one unbroken string sets the min-content width and pushes the trailing column off a phone.

meta.$description: The one thing that varies down the list — a date, a status. Forty identical rows are forty identical rows; something has to differ or the eye has nowhere to land.

style.$description: Bare rows, or a bounded panel of them.

panel.$description: Bordered and divided — for rows that are managed rather than read.

selected.$description: The row you are on — the credential you signed in with. Marked with a badge and not only a tint: it is the one row whose action would sign you out.

a11y.note: `<ul>` by default, `<ol>` when the position is data — a ranked board loses its meaning the moment one row is filtered out of an unordered list. Either way it carries a label, so the count is announced. A per-row action needs the row's NAME in its accessible name: nine buttons all called 'Revoke' tell a screen-reader user nothing about which one they are on. Where that action is destructive it wears the danger variant here AND in its confirm dialog.
